newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Sept 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Confronted at a three-and-a-half-hour shareholders meeting about BHP's decision to purchase Magma Copper for A$3.2 billion, BHP chairman Brian Loton said the investment would come good in the long run. Page 1.

ANZ Banking Group and National Australia Bank are about to launch their biggest assault on the world banking market since their ill-fated ventures in the 1980s. This time the moves have the backing of a strong headhunting drive and the launch of powerful global banking units. Page 1.

The manufacturing sector has suffered its sixth bad quarter in a row, a survey released yesterday by the Australian Chamber of Manufactures said. Lagging in economic growth, the industry was hopeful that the usually strong Christmas quarter would help stop declines in production and profit. Page 3.

The Motor Trades Association of Australia and the Australian Automobile Dealers Association have joined unions in a boycott of the Industry Commission's review of assistance to car manufacturers after 2000, accusing the commission of social and economic irresponsibility and prejudging the inquiry outcome. Page 3.

Australian Gaslight Company proposal to end its monopoly control over the State's gas pipeline distribution system has angered major New South Wales gas users and potential new gas suppliers, who believe the company is manipulating the gas industry eform process in order to maintain its State gas monopoly. Page 23.

Unable to wait for new radio licences any longer and unable to afford the licences of its preferred option, city-based radios, radio investment group DMG Radio Australia has purchased some regional radio assets. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Tensions at Australian National Industries Ltd intensified yesterday when director Peter Joseph filed a notice with ANI seeking to remove fellow director Ross Palmer from the board in time for next month's shareholder meeting. In an explanatory memo to other directors, Joseph also indicated deputy chairman Fred Smith should go. Page 35.

Australia's biggest investor, the AMP Society, is expected to announce a major shareholding in the restructured Ansett International later this week, a move which would see AMP becoming a significant player in the airline industry. Page 35.

BHP chairman Brian Loton told the annual meeting in Sydney yesterday shareholders could expect further market disturbances for its fledgling BHP copper division, but justified the A$3.2 billion acquisition of the loss-making United States-based Magma Coper Co assets as a "strategy still relevant". Page 35.

According to the results of an ongoing Insurance and Superannuation Commission review program of super fund trustees, which aims to cover all approved trustees and industry funds within three years, fraud and incompetence among trustees have reached alarmng levels, with shortcomings existing in five per cent of all super funds. Page 35.

Chemical and plastic producer ICI Australia Ltd has announced it will dump its auditor of 80 years, Price Waterhouse, and bring in KPMG to audit its accounts - a strong indication ICI is preparing to merge with its British parent, ICI plc, who also utilises the services of KPMG. Page 37.

National carrier Telstra yesterday unveiled an advertising campaign aimed at thirtysomething professionals, the group identified as most likely to defect as a result of Optus Vision's entry to its A$5 billion local telephone market. Telstra has also asked industry regulator Austel to arbitrate a dispute with Optus over who should pay the cost of a system that allows customers to retain their phone numbers if they change phone companies. Page 37.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

BHP directors faced a barrage of criticism at their three-and-a-half-hour annual general meeting in Sydney yesterday, with shareholders airing their frustration at the 'Big Australian's' profit and environmental performances and its failure to turn major acquisitions into substantial profit centres. Page 29.

ANI director Peter Joseph, in his capacity as a shareholder, brought the company's ongoing boardroom battle to a head yesterday when he gave notice to ANI of his resolution for the upcoming annual general meeting on October 21 to sack fellow director Ross Palmer. Page 29.

National carrier Telstra yesterday ruled out sparking a price war in response to Optus Vision's dramatic entry into the local telephone market, saying it would rather attempt to retain its customers by promoting a range of services that will largely prove price competitive to Optus Vision, rather than focusing on price alone. Page 31.

Following a rumoured show of support from John Singleton Advertising , which recently moved its five per cent stake in the Ten Network from a non-current asset to a current asset, the proposal to create a listed trust unit to allow key shareholders in Ten to sell out appears set to proceed. Page 31.

The former head of the Austereo Network, Paul Thompson, re-entered the Australian radio scene yesterday when DMG Radio Australia, a subsidiary of the United Kingdom-based Daily Mail and General Trust Group DMOG.L created seven months ago, announced the purchase of regional operator Broadcast Media. Page 31.

According to KPMG's 10th annual Insurance Industry Survey, the market value of the life insurance sector is expected to rocket to A$10 billion within the next four years, largely due to the public listing of major players, including the AMP Society. Page 1.
THE AGE

At a marathon annual meeting in Sydney yesterday, attended by more than 3,000 shareholders, BHP chairman Brian Loton defended the group's A$3.2 billion acquisition of United States-based Magma Copper, as he attempted to appease shareholders' dissatisfactin with the group's recent profit slide and the fall in BHP's share price. Page C1.

The future of Avalon airport, north east of Geelong, which has been for sale for over a year, was secured yesterday with the announcement that Lindsay Fox's Linfox Transport group and British airports manager Serco have emerged as the Federal Government's preferred buyer. Page C1.

According to a poll taken by stockbroker J.B. Were, the corporate broker to BHP, of its private clients, only 18 per cent of 320 small shareholders were dissatisfied with the BHP board's medium to long-term performance. Page C1.

Resolute Samantha chief executive Michael Carrick said yesterday that over the next two years his company would increase its exploration budget from about A$15 million to A$40 million, becoming one of Australia's largest explorers. Page C2.

With John Singleton Advertising agreeing to sell its five per cent shareholding in the Ten Network, it seems certain that the Ten Network will list on the Australian Stock Exchange as a single purpose unit. Page C2.

The energy sector, which is doing so well at the moment, lifted the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday, pushing the All Ordinaries Index 9.5 points higher to 2228.7 after is dropped to 2213.4 earlier on. Page C2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-1 9373-1800
